chapter: Arranging craft, ownership and the business
title: Starving for jazz on television and the thrill of discovery
summary: As kids they caught jazz references on TV like Sid Caesar and Peter Gunn; discovery was scarcer and more joyful then.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Oh yeah, and still are. Well you remember the old Sid Caesar bit when he was Progress Hornsby and he had the radar antenna on the bell of his tenor, and that’s in case he got too close to the melody.
Oh that’s good. I wasn’t aware of that.

Oh Progress Hornsby, you know as kids we didn’t have any place to go to see jazz, but once in a while there’d be a jazz reference on television like Sid Caesar doing Progress Hornsby. You know we were hungry for anything that, you know, related to jazz. And there was nothing on TV. Then Peter Gunn came out and boy that was an explosion right there.
Isn’t that interesting that when you compare it nowadays to everything is available at any time, how much joy we took in those discoveries.
And that they came in few and far between, or spending hours listening to the record, to the radio, hoping they’ll play that song again.

Yeah. You know I still hear things and I think wow, what could they do there. You know I’ll hear it once on the radio and then try to find it so I can try and figure out what they did. There’s some really good, there’s some talented people out there playing and writing. There’s no question about it.
